svg.title: Interval the difference, not the two numbers
svg.desc: A whiteboard sketch showing a population cloud with a sample scooped from it and an inference arrow back; the bootstrap drawn as four resampled rows with the duplicated values marked in red feeding a histogram whose 2.5 and 97.5 percent cut points are dashed in; two model confidence intervals for F1 of 0.9231 and 0.9518 drawn as overlapping bars with the conclusion that they are not significantly different crossed out; the paired difference interval of plus 0.0287 with bounds 0.0074 to 0.0538 drawn entirely to the right of zero and P of B better than A at 99.66 percent; and a struck-through list of the three things a p-value is not.
svg.text: Interval the difference, not the two numbers
every number you compute is a draw
POPULATION
SAMPLE
inference
run the study again and every number moves.
the bootstrap: resample your own sample, WITH REPLACEMENT
your one sample
red = drawn twice. That is what "with replacement" means.
with replacement
TWO OVERLAPPING INTERVALS ARE NOT A TEST
model A F1 0.9231
model B F1 0.9518
"they overlap, so not significantly different" - NO.
put the interval on the DIFFERENCE instead
paired difference
entirely above zero. P(B > A) = 99.66%
and what a p-value is NOT
the probability the null is true
the probability the result is due to chance
the size of the effect
it IS: P(data this extreme or more | the null is true)
overlapping CIs is the most common
statistical error in ML papers. Always
interval the DIFFERENCE, and pair the
folds.
...and if you peek every day? -> Module 4
